groups.decision: Convert a positive Euler-product free energy to an exact-size coefficient lower bound
groups.shortestRoute: The upper bound is a one-parameter generating-function estimate. The matching lower bound uses independent geometric multiplicities, concentration inside a size window and the injection obtained by adding ones.
groups.hypotheses: Integer exclusion modulus at least2 guarantees part1 remains allowed; unordered positive parts may repeat; t>0 makes the product and expectations finite.
groups.proofReview: The integrable logarithmic endpoint and exponential tail justify the product Riemann sum. Separate mean and variance Riemann sums are used, avoiding differentiation of an asymptotic relation. Their nonnegative expansions give the stated zeta2 moments. For fixed epsilon, the mean sits distance proportional to n from both window edges and variance is O(n^(3/2)), so Chebyshev gives window probability tending to1. The exact probability identity and adding-ones injection then provide the required coefficient lower bound. The source inequality has the correct exponential direction.
groups.neighbor: Shares product background with Lambert singularity, but exact-size coefficient extraction requires a new converse argument. Different excluded moduli change the allowed lattice density.
